A lithography method comprises: providing a substrate with a target region; determining a topology of the substrate within the target region; determining a correcting telecentricity profile based on the topology of the substrate within the target region; providing a radiation beam; and projecting the radiation beam onto the target region of the substrate so as to form an image on the substrate. The radiation beam is such that a net direction of the total radiation received by one or more points in the target region of the substrate is chosen in dependence on the determined correcting telecentricity. The correcting telecentricity profile is such that the net direction of the total radiation received by at least one point in the target region of the substrate is chosen so as to at least partially correct for an overlay error introduced by a curvature of a surface of the substrate at said point.

outputs.L3:
The method comprises providing a substrate that includes a target region intended for lithographic processing. Before the projection step is carried out, the topology of the substrate within the target region is determined. This may involve measuring the height profile or surface shape of the substrate in and around the area where an image is to be formed.

Based on the measured substrate topology, a correcting telecentricity profile is calculated. The correcting telecentricity profile represents an adjustment to the direction of the radiation beam that is selected to compensate, at least in part, for overlay errors that may arise due to curvature or height variations of the substrate surface.

A radiation beam is then projected onto the target region so as to form an image on the substrate. During this projection, the direction of the radiation beam is adjusted in accordance with the calculated correcting telecentricity profile. By modifying the beam direction in this way, overlay errors caused by substrate surface curvature can be partially corrected, thereby improving the alignment accuracy of the lithographic process.
outputs.L4:
A lithography method is provided for improving pattern placement accuracy when exposing a substrate that is not perfectly flat. In the method, the topology of the substrate is determined in or around a target region to be exposed. The topology information may include height variations, local slope, curvature, or other surface-shape characteristics of the substrate, and may be obtained using a level sensor, interferometric sensor, focus sensor, pre-exposure measurement system, or stored metrology data.

Based on the determined substrate topology, a correcting telecentricity profile is calculated for the projection of a patterned radiation beam onto the target region. The telecentricity profile defines how the net propagation direction of the radiation beam should be modified at one or more positions across the exposure field. In particular, where the substrate surface is curved or tilted relative to an expected reference plane, the radiation beam can be directed so that its incidence better corresponds to the local orientation or shape of the substrate surface.

During exposure, the lithographic apparatus adjusts the beam’s net direction at one or more points in the target region according to the correcting telecentricity profile. This adjustment may be achieved, for example, by controlling one or more optical elements in the projection system, by modifying the illumination or projection settings, or by applying field-dependent corrections that influence the direction of the projected radiation. The correction may be applied globally across the field or locally at selected points, depending on the measured substrate topology and the expected overlay error.

By compensating at least partially for overlay errors caused by substrate curvature, the method improves the accuracy with which a pattern is imaged onto the substrate. This is particularly useful for substrates that exhibit wafer bow, local height variations, processed-layer topography, or other non-flatness effects. As a result, the projected pattern can be better aligned with previously formed features, reducing overlay error and improving device yield and lithographic performance.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it carries surprising importance. It is called a definite article, and its job is to point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that both the speaker and listener understand.

This simple word helps create clarity. It turns general ideas into specific ones: “the sun,” “the ocean,” “the future.” It can make something feel familiar, important, or unique. For example, “the moment” sounds more meaningful than just “a moment.”

Although “the” often goes unnoticed, it shapes how we understand sentences. It guides attention, gives context, and helps language feel complete. In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a powerful role in communication.

**Title:** Systems and Methods for Overlay Control by Topography-Dependent Modification of Exposure-Beam Telecentricity

**Abstract**

A lithographic exposure system and method are provided for improving overlay accuracy in semiconductor device manufacturing. In one embodiment, topographic information associated with one or more target regions of a substrate is obtained prior to exposure. The topographic information may include local height, slope, curvature, film-stack-induced deformation, or pattern-density-dependent topography. Based at least in part on the topographic information, a desired telecentricity profile of an exposure beam is determined. The lithographic apparatus is then controlled to modify a telecentricity characteristic of the exposure beam, such as a chief-ray angle distribution across an exposure field or within selected sub-regions of the field. The modified telecentricity profile compensates for overlay error components caused by interaction between non-planar wafer topography and the projection optics, focus condition, or resist imaging process. The exposure is thereafter performed using the modified telecentricity profile, thereby reducing local and/or field-level overlay error.

---

## Patent-Style Description

### Field of the Invention

The present disclosure relates generally to semiconductor lithography, and more particularly to systems and methods for improving overlay performance by controlling a telecentricity profile of an exposure beam in accordance with wafer topography associated with target regions to be patterned.

### Background

In semiconductor manufacturing, overlay accuracy between successive patterned layers is a critical parameter affecting device yield and performance. As device geometries shrink, overlay budgets become increasingly stringent. Conventional overlay correction techniques may include wafer alignment, stage positioning correction, lens distortion correction, dose correction, focus correction, and field-by-field or wafer-level correction models.

However, certain overlay errors arise from local wafer topography. For example, variations in substrate height, film thickness, local pattern density, etch or deposition non-uniformity, chemical-mechanical polishing effects, and device-region topography can cause local displacement of aerial-image placement or resist-image formation. Such errors may not be fully corrected by conventional alignment or distortion models, particularly where the errors vary within an exposure field or correspond to target-region-specific height profiles.

Projection systems are generally designed to be substantially telecentric at the wafer plane. Nevertheless, a controlled deviation from nominal telecentricity may be used to intentionally shift image placement as a function of local wafer height or topographic slope. Existing systems typically do not determine or apply a spatially varying telecentricity profile based on measured or predicted topography of the actual target regions to be exposed.

Accordingly, there is a need for improved lithographic methods and apparatus capable of compensating for topography-induced overlay error by modifying exposure-beam telecentricity in accordance with wafer topography.

### Summary

In one aspect, a method of patterning a substrate includes obtaining topographic data corresponding to a target region of the substrate, determining from the topographic data a telecentricity correction for an exposure beam, adjusting one or more optical or illumination parameters of a lithographic apparatus to produce a modified telecentricity profile of the exposure beam, and exposing the target region using the modified telecentricity profile.

In another aspect, a lithographic apparatus includes a projection optical system, an adjustable beam-control element configured to modify an angular characteristic of an exposure beam at a substrate plane, a substrate support, and a controller. The controller is configured to receive topographic information for at least one target region of a substrate, calculate a telecentricity profile based on the topographic information and an overlay-error model, and actuate the adjustable beam-control element to implement the telecentricity profile during exposure.

In yet another aspect, a non-transitory computer-readable medium stores instructions that, when executed by a controller of a lithographic apparatus, cause the controller to obtain target-region topography data, determine a spatially varying chief-ray angle profile configured to reduce topography-induced overlay error, and control an exposure system to expose a substrate using the spatially varying chief-ray angle profile.

### Detailed Description

Embodiments of the invention provide a lithographic exposure technique in which an exposure beam is intentionally provided with a selected telecentricity profile based on wafer topography. As used herein, “telecentricity profile” may refer to one or more angular characteristics of the exposure beam at or near the substrate plane, including chief-ray angle, ray bundle tilt, pupil asymmetry, field-dependent angular distribution, or a deviation from nominal telecentricity as a function of position within an exposure field.

In some embodiments, the wafer topography is obtained using a level sensor, interferometric height sensor, scatterometry-based metrology, optical profilometry, atomic force microscopy, previous-layer metrology, process simulation, or a combination thereof. The topographic information may be measured directly before exposure, obtained from a process database, predicted from pattern-density information, or generated by combining measured wafer-shape information with modeled intra-field topography.

The target region may comprise an entire exposure field, a die, a portion of a die, a product-device region, an overlay-mark region, or a plurality of sub-regions within a field. The topographic information may include absolute height, relative height, height gradient, local slope, curvature, step height, film-stack thickness variation, or spatial frequency components of topography.

A controller may process the topographic information using an overlay-error model. The overlay-error model may relate a local height or slope of the substrate to a lateral image displacement caused by a non-zero chief-ray angle. For example, a lateral placement shift may be approximated as a function of local wafer height and beam angle. By selecting an appropriate telecentricity deviation, the controller may introduce a compensating lateral shift that offsets topography-induced overlay error. In other embodiments, the model may include resist effects, focus-dependent image placement, lens aberrations, scanner slit dynamics, stage motion, illumination mode, numerical aperture, mask three-dimensional effects, and process-dependent bias.

The determined telecentricity profile may be uniform for a field, vary between fields, vary along a scanning direction, vary across a slit, or vary within sub-field regions. In a scanning lithography apparatus, the telecentricity profile may be dynamically adjusted during scanning such that different portions of the target region are exposed with different chief-ray angles. In a step-and-repeat apparatus, the telecentricity profile may be adjusted on a field-by-field basis.

The telecentricity profile may be implemented using one or more adjustable beam-control elements. Such elements may include a tiltable optical element, deformable mirror, adaptive lens, wedge plate, pupil filter, pupil-shaping element, illumination source actuator, reticle-stage or wafer-stage tilt control, projection-lens actuator, adjustable aperture, spatial light modulator, or other optical component capable of changing an angular distribution of the exposure beam at the wafer plane.

In some embodiments, the controller determines a target telecentricity profile that minimizes a cost function. The cost function may include predicted overlay residuals, focus error, critical-dimension uniformity, image contrast, aberration limits, scanner actuator constraints, and process-window metrics. The selected profile may therefore represent an optimized tradeoff between overlay improvement and other lithographic performance parameters.

After exposure, overlay metrology may be performed. The measured overlay residuals may be fed back to update the topography-to-telecentricity model. In this manner, subsequent wafers, lots, or layers may be exposed using refined telecentricity corrections. Feedforward and feedback correction may be combined.

### Exemplary Claims

**1.** A method of lithographically patterning a substrate, the method comprising:  
obtaining topographic information corresponding to a target region of the substrate;  
determining, based at least in part on the topographic information, a telecentricity profile for an exposure beam;  
adjusting a lithographic apparatus to provide the exposure beam with the telecentricity profile; and  
exposing the target region with the exposure beam having the telecentricity profile,  
wherein the telecentricity profile is selected to reduce overlay error associated with the topographic information.

**2.** The method of claim 1, wherein the topographic information comprises at least one of a local height, a height gradient, a slope, a curvature, a film thickness variation, or a pattern-density-dependent topography of the target region.

**3.** The method of claim 1, wherein determining the telecentricity profile comprises calculating a chief-ray angle distribution at a substrate plane.

**4.** The method of claim 1, wherein the telecentricity profile varies spatially across an exposure field.

**5.** The method of claim 1, wherein the telecentricity profile varies dynamically during a scanning exposure.

**6.** The method of claim 1, wherein adjusting the lithographic apparatus comprises actuating at least one of a tiltable optical element, a deformable mirror, an adaptive lens, a wedge element, a pupil-shaping element, an illumination source actuator, a reticle-stage actuator, a substrate-stage actuator, or a projection-lens actuator.

**7.** The method of claim 1, wherein determining the telecentricity profile comprises applying an overlay-error model that relates the topographic information to a predicted image-placement error.

**8.** The method of claim 7, wherein the overlay-error model includes at least one of lens aberration data, focus data, resist-process data, illumination settings, mask three-dimensional effect data, or stage-positioning data.

**9.** The method of claim 1, further comprising measuring overlay after exposing the target region and updating a model used to determine the telecentricity profile based on the measured overlay.

**10.** The method of claim 1, wherein the target region comprises a plurality of sub-regions, and wherein different sub-regions are exposed using different telecentricity corrections.

**11.** A lithographic apparatus comprising:  
a projection optical system configured to project a patterned exposure beam onto a target region of a substrate;  
an adjustable beam-control element configured to modify a telecentricity characteristic of the patterned exposure beam at the substrate; and  
a controller configured to:  
receive topographic information corresponding to the target region;  
determine, based on the topographic information, a telecentricity profile configured to reduce overlay error; and  
control the adjustable beam-control element to provide the patterned exposure beam with the telecentricity profile during exposure of the target region.

**12.** The lithographic apparatus of claim 11, wherein the adjustable beam-control element comprises at least one of a tiltable lens, a tiltable mirror, a deformable optical element, an adaptive optical element, a wedge plate, a pupil filter, or a spatial light modulator.

**13.** The lithographic apparatus of claim 11, wherein the controller is configured to determine a spatially varying chief-ray angle profile across an exposure slit.

**14.** The lithographic apparatus of claim 11, further comprising a topography sensor configured to measure height information of the substrate prior to exposure.

**15.** The lithographic apparatus of claim 11, wherein the controller is configured to dynamically alter the telecentricity profile during scanning of the target region.

**16.** A non-transitory computer-readable storage medium storing instructions which, when executed by one or more processors associated with a lithographic apparatus, cause the one or more processors to:  
obtain target-region topography data for a substrate;  
determine a telecentricity correction based on the target-region topography data and a predicted overlay-error response; and  
generate control signals for one or more optical actuators to modify an exposure-beam telecentricity profile during lithographic exposure of the substrate.

**17.** The non-transitory computer-readable storage medium of claim 16, wherein the telecentricity correction comprises a spatially varying chief-ray angle distribution.

**18.** The non-transitory computer-readable storage medium of claim 16, wherein the instructions further cause the one or more processors to update the predicted overlay-error response using post-exposure overlay metrology.

### Technical Effect

By adapting the telecentricity profile of the exposure beam to local or regional wafer topography, embodiments of the invention compensate for topography-induced image-placement shifts that otherwise contribute to overlay error. The technique may provide improved intra-field overlay, die-to-die overlay, and wafer-level overlay without requiring additional patterning steps, and may be integrated with existing scanner control, focus control, and overlay correction frameworks.
